page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.2-8 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance configured with 4 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.25 GHz, this instance allocates two physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, providing two threads per core. The resources use dedicated CPU allocation rather than burstable or shared scheduling, maintaining consistent computational availability for running processes.

The configuration establishes a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, equating to 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled with the server, necessitating external block storage attachments for any persistent file systems or database operations. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No discrete graphics processors or hardware accelerators are included on this instance type.

Because the server omits local NVMe drives and avoids larger memory footprints, resource density remains focused primarily on processing threads. This provides qualitative cost efficiency for compute-leaning applications that do not require high memory-per-core allocations. The VM.Standard.E3.Flex.2-8 is well suited for workloads such as distributed build and CI/CD runners, containerized web services, batch compute tasks, and lightweight application middleware.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.2-8 is a compute-focused instance built on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor running at 2.25 GHz. It provisions 4 vCPUs across 2 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 8.0 GB of system memory. This results in a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core, targeting compute-oriented workloads without excessive RAM overhead. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network block volumes for persistent disk needs, and features one complimentary public IPv4 address with zero dedicated GPUs. By directing resource allocation toward dedicated AMD processor cores rather than oversized memory arrays or local disks, this configuration maintains high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-centric workloads. It is appropriate for CI/CD pipelines, containerized microservices, batch processing, and general web serving.
